name: Jahangir
contribution: As Mughal emperor, Jahangir authorized the campaigns that brought more of Bengal under imperial control and gave his name to the new provincial capital, Jahangirnagar (Dhaka).
context: During his reign, Islam Khan Chishti moved the Mughal capital of Bengal to Dhaka in 1610 and directed campaigns against resistance networks in the Bhati region. The period connected imperial expansion with a new administrative center.
impact: The Dhaka-centered reorganization strengthened Mughal administration in eastern Bengal, while the campaigns of Jahangir’s reign helped complete the transition from contested frontier to provincial governance.
highlight: The Mughal emperor whose reign saw Bengal’s capital move to Dhaka, renamed Jahangirnagar in his honor.
seoTitle: Jahangir and Bengal: The Rise of Jahangirnagar
seoDescription: Learn how Mughal emperor Jahangir’s reign shaped Bengal’s consolidation and the 1610 transfer of the provincial capital to Dhaka, renamed Jahangirnagar.
shortAnswer: Jahangir was the Mughal emperor during the 1610 shift of Bengal’s provincial capital to Dhaka, which was renamed Jahangirnagar in his honor.
